title: ParVL: Parallel Scaling and Expandable Compute Allocation for Multimodal LLMs
headline: ParVL: Parallel Scaling for Multimodal LLMs with Dynamic Compute Allocation
tldr: ParVL introduces a parallel scaling framework that allows separate, task‑specific allocation of compute resources between vision and language modules in multimodal LLMs. This reduces memory and latency overhead while enabling flexible, efficient inference across diverse applications.
significance: By decoupling vision and language compute budgets, ParVL offers a scalable, low‑latency alternative to monolithic MLLM scaling, facilitating real‑time multimodal AI.

title: WorldCup Arena: Prospective, Leakage-Free Evaluation of Frontier LLMs on a Live Tournament
headline: Live Forecasting: Evaluating LLMs During the 2026 FIFA World Cup
tldr: Researchers tested six cutting‑edge LLMs in real time over the 2026 FIFA World Cup, measuring their predictive accuracy without relying on post‑event data. The study demonstrates a novel, leakage‑free benchmark that captures true forecasting performance.
significance: This work establishes the first live, prospective benchmark for LLM forecasting, revealing how well models generalize to unfolding events.

title: TurnSight: Turn-Level Hindsight Self-Distillation for Tool-Integrated Reasoning
headline: TurnSight: Fine-Grained Self-Distillation Boosts Tool-Integrated Reasoning for Complex Tasks in LLMs
tldr: TurnSight introduces turn-level hindsight self-distillation, providing dense credit signals during iterative tool use. This approach improves long-horizon reasoning in large language models without requiring trajectory-level supervision.
significance: By enabling fine-grained learning signals, TurnSight advances the efficiency and accuracy of tool-integrated reasoning systems.

title: Calibrating Trustworthiness: Co-Designing Metrics and Visualizations for Evaluating LLMs in Education
headline: Co-Designing Trust Metrics to Evaluate LLMs for Educational Use Effectively
tldr: This study proposes a structured framework for assessing LLM trustworthiness in educational contexts, integrating pedagogical alignment metrics. By co-designing visualizations and benchmarks, it enables educators and developers to identify and mitigate potential disruptions.
significance: It bridges the gap between technical LLM evaluation and pedagogical needs, fostering safer AI integration in learning environments.

title: Localizing polymers promotes the centre-mode elastic instability
headline: Localizing Polymers Amplifies Centre-Mode Elastic Instability in Dilute Solutions
tldr: The centre-mode elastic instability can arise without inertia in dilute polymer flows. This study shows that nonuniform polymer distributions, such as a polymer-laden core between solvent streams, significantly enhance the instability.
significance: Understanding how polymer localization drives instability informs design of microfluidic devices and improves control of polymer processing.

title: Semantic Bundling: Interactive Node and Edge Bundling to Simplify Knowledge Graphs using Large Language Models
headline: Semantic Bundling: Interactive Node and Edge Bundling for Knowledge Graph Simplification with LLMs
tldr: We introduce Semantic Bundling, a visual analytics method that uses large language models to guide interactive node and edge bundling in knowledge graphs, making large corpora easier to interpret. The approach preserves semantic relationships while reducing visual clutter, enabling analysts to explore document collections more efficiently.
significance: Semantic Bundling bridges LLM-driven semantic understanding with graph visualization, offering a scalable solution for interpreting complex knowledge graphs.

title: PAST-Bench: Benchmarking the Foundations of Recursive Self-Improvement in Personal Agents
headline: PAST-Bench: Measuring Recursive Self-Improvement in Personal AI Agents for Future Capabilities
tldr: PAST-Bench evaluates whether personal AI agents can turn their accumulated experience into better future behavior. The benchmark tracks preference retention, task history, tool usage, and skill learning across sessions to systematically test recursive self-improvement.
significance: This work provides the first systematic test of recursive self-improvement in personal agents, offering a foundation for future AI safety and capability research.

title: Test-Time Scaling in Reasoning LLMs: Inference Regimes, Evaluation, and Reproducibility
headline: Test-Time Scaling Boosts Reasoning in Large Language Models by Extending Inference Algorithms
tldr: Large language models can solve harder reasoning tasks by scaling inference time. Various algorithms—trajectory extension, candidate sampling, partial state search—improve performance, but their statistical properties differ.
significance: This work clarifies how inference regimes affect reasoning accuracy, guiding reproducible benchmarking of LLMs.

title: Agogic: Performance-Timed Music Tokens for LLM-Native Text-to-Symbolic-Music Generation
headline: Agogic: Evaluating Music Tokenization Impact on LLM-Based Text-to-Music Generation Across Seven Representations
tldr: The study isolates the effect of music tokenization by swapping representations while keeping the Qwen3.5 model, data, and decoding constant. Results show that token choice significantly alters performance, with some tokenizations approaching the model-free ceiling.
significance: It provides the first quantitative benchmark of tokenization strategies for symbolic music generation, guiding future LLM design.

title: When Attention Goes Blind: Numerical Failure in ALiBi Positional Encodings
headline: Floating-Point Underflow Undermines ALiBi Positional Encoding in Large Language Models
tldr: The study uncovers that ALiBi’s linear bias scaling can underflow floating-point precision, causing many attention weights to zero out and rendering some heads partially blind. It analyzes the impact, proposes four mitigation strategies, and demonstrates the issue in state-of-the-art models.
significance: This finding highlights a critical, previously overlooked vulnerability in a widely used positional encoding technique, affecting the reliability of modern foundation models.

title: WorldExam: Benchmarking World Models from Apparent Appearance to Inherent Reactivity
headline: Benchmarking World Models: From Video Appearance to Inherent Reactivity Evaluation
tldr: Controllable video generation models are being used as world models, requiring evaluation beyond visual fidelity to include the model's ability to infer and generate plausible world reactions. The paper proposes a benchmark that tests both appearance and inherent reactivity of such models.
significance: This benchmark advances the assessment of generative models by incorporating dynamic reasoning, enabling more realistic and useful AI-driven simulations.

title: Discovery of the Distant, Ultra-Faint Milky Way Satellite Aquarius IV with the Vera C. Rubin Observatory Early Data Preview 2
headline: Discovery of Ultra-Faint Milky Way Satellite Aquarius IV Using Vera C. Rubin Observatory Data
tldr: Astronomers identified Aquarius IV, a faint Milky Way satellite, with 8σ significance in Rubin Observatory Early Data Preview 2 and confirmed it at 6σ using Dark Energy Camera imagery. This marks the first satellite found using Rubin data, expanding our knowledge of the Galaxy’s outskirts.
significance: It demonstrates the Rubin Observatory’s power to uncover extremely faint celestial objects, opening new avenues for studying the Milky Way’s structure.

title: Bridging Artificial Intelligence and Power Systems Education Using a Hands-On Executable Framework
headline: Hands‑On AI Framework Bridges Power Systems Education Gap
tldr: The paper introduces an executable AI framework that makes power system modeling, forecasting, and control accessible to students and interdisciplinary researchers. It provides reusable modules and hands‑on exercises, filling a gap left by specialized, non‑reusable AI studies.
significance: By offering a reusable, hands‑on AI toolkit, the framework democratizes power systems education and accelerates interdisciplinary innovation.

title: VR3D: View-Robust 3D Representation Learning for Aerial-Ground Person Re-Identification
headline: VR3D: Robust 3D Representation for Aerial‑Ground Person Re‑Identification Across Viewpoints
tldr: Aerial‑ground person re‑identification suffers from viewpoint variations causing occlusion and deformation. VR3D introduces a view‑robust 3D representation learning framework that decouples viewpoint bias, improving cross‑platform matching.
significance: By learning view‑invariant 3D features, VR3D enables more reliable person re‑identification between aerial and ground cameras, a critical capability for surveillance and search‑and‑rescue operations.

title: SDSS-V Local Volume Mapper (LVM): Dithered Data Cube Reconstruction with 3dcubegen
headline: Reconstructing SDSS-V LVM Data Cubes: Dithered Observations and 3dcubegen Techniques
tldr: The SDSS-V Local Volume Mapper uses multiple dithered observations to achieve full spatial coverage of nearby galaxies. The 3dcubegen software reconstructs these observations into high-resolution data cubes for scientific analysis.
significance: This approach enhances spatial sampling and spectral depth, enabling unprecedented studies of the Milky Way and nearby galaxies.

title: Staying Productive Under the Palm Trees. On Graded Coeffect Typing in the Tropical Semiring
headline: Modeling Time and Productivity with Graded Coeffect Typing in the Tropical Semiring
tldr: We present a graded coeffect typing system that uses the tropical semiring over natural numbers to model time delays in function parameters. This approach guarantees productivity of well-typed programs while faithfully representing temporal availability of resources.
significance: This work provides a rigorous framework for reasoning about time-dependent resource availability in functional programming, bridging type theory and temporal logic.

title: onepot-Bench 0: towards lab-aware in silico chemistry benchmarks
headline: onepot-Bench 0: Lab-Aware In Silico Chemistry Benchmark for Language Models
tldr: The onepot-Bench 0 benchmark evaluates language models on laboratory science tasks such as experiment planning, execution, and analysis. It addresses the challenge of measuring both problem-solving skills and domain intuition required for in silico chemistry.
significance: It provides a standardized, lab-aware test for assessing LLMs in chemistry, guiding future model development.

title: Exact Likelihood and Sampling for Riemannian Gaussian Distributions on Correlation Matrices
headline: Exact Likelihood for Riemannian Gaussian Models on Correlation Matrices
tldr: The paper introduces a proper Riemannian Gaussian distribution for full‑rank correlation matrices, deriving exact score equations and finite radial moments. It also presents quotient‑affine geometry techniques to handle normalization and scale profiling.
significance: It provides a mathematically rigorous framework for probabilistic modeling of correlation structures with practical implications for statistical inference.

title: Testing for subgroup treatment effect consistency in the Cox model
headline: Assessing Subgroup Consistency of Treatment Effects in Cox Models: A Practical Guide
tldr: This article introduces a new approach for testing whether treatment effects are consistent across patient subgroups in survival analysis. It extends conventional interaction tests by evaluating the magnitude of differences rather than just equality.
significance: The method enables clinicians to determine if population-level efficacy can be reliably applied to specific subpopulations, improving personalized treatment decisions.

title: Optimal Quantum de Finetti Theorems via Argmax Rounding
headline: Optimal Quantum de Finetti Bounds Achieved
tldr: We prove tight finite de Finetti bounds for bosonic states, achieving a 1/(N-1) scaling in trace norm, and extend to arbitrary exchangeable states.
significance: This resolves a long-standing open problem in quantum information theory.

title: CAPEval: A Decoupled Caption Evaluation across Understanding and Generation
headline: CAPEval: Separating Caption Coverage and Reliability for Better Multimodal Evaluation
tldr: CAPEval introduces a decoupled framework that separately measures how much visual content a caption describes and how well the image supports those claims. This approach provides clearer diagnostics for both multimodal understanding models and text‑to‑image generation systems.
significance: By disentangling coverage and reliability, CAPEval enables more precise model improvement and fairer benchmarking across vision‑language tasks.

title: The Condition-Number Barrier in Sparse Least Squares
headline: Condition-Number Barrier Proven for Sparse Least Squares Under Small-Set Expansion Hypothesis
tldr: The authors establish the conjectured lower bound on the dependence on the restricted condition number for sparse least‑squares objectives, assuming the randomized exact‑volume Small‑Set Expansion Hypothesis. This result shows that no polynomial‑time algorithm can beat the linear dependence on the condition number in this setting.
significance: It confirms a long‑standing conjecture, delineating the limits of efficient sparse convex optimization.

title: GradCuit: Credit-Assigned Gradient Flow Enables Robust and Interpretable Test-Time Latent Reasoning
headline: GradCuit: Credit-Assigned Gradient Flow for Robust Test-Time Latent Reasoning in Large Language Models
tldr: GradCuit introduces a credit-assigned gradient flow that directly links latent state updates to reasoning steps, improving LLM outputs without retraining. By assigning credit at the token level, it offers clearer interpretability and robust performance across diverse prompts.
significance: This method enhances LLM reasoning by providing transparent, test-time optimization that preserves model weights and improves accuracy.

title: Toward Robust and 3D-Aware RGB-NIR Imaging in the Dark
headline: 3D-Aware RGB-NIR Imaging Boosts Low-Light Performance with Robust Neural Modeling
tldr: This study introduces a 3D-aware neural framework for RGB-NIR low-light imaging, improving robustness across varied scenarios. By integrating depth cues, the method surpasses traditional paired-data approaches, offering better enhancement in dark environments.
significance: It demonstrates that incorporating 3D structure into RGB-NIR fusion yields more reliable low-light enhancement, potentially benefiting surveillance and autonomous systems.

title: Emulating the nonlinear effects of modified gravity on the matter power spectrum for reconstruction
headline: Fast Neural Emulation of Nonlinear Modified Gravity Effects on Matter Power Spectrum
tldr: We build a neural-network emulator to predict the nonlinear matter power spectrum in modified gravity models, drastically speeding up likelihood evaluations. This enables efficient exploration of high-dimensional parameter spaces and improves model-independent reconstruction of MG functions.
significance: The emulator reduces computational cost by orders of magnitude, allowing comprehensive testing of modified gravity theories against cosmological data.

title: Dark Photons from Perturbative Decay of a Misaligned Higgs Field
headline: Dark Photons from Misaligned Higgs Decay: A Predictive Dark Matter Model
tldr: We propose that dark photons arise from the perturbative decay of a misaligned dark Higgs field generated during inflation. The resulting relic abundance is tightly constrained by structure formation and isocurvature limits, offering a testable dark matter scenario.
significance: This framework links inflationary physics to observable dark matter properties, providing a clear target for future cosmological probes.

title: Scaling Properties of Text Conditioning in Visual Generation
headline: Scaling Text Conditioning in Diffusion Models: Structured Language Drives Loss
tldr: The study measures how diffusion loss scales with the amount of structured language in prompts, revealing that more structured prompts lead to lower loss. This finding challenges previous assumptions that token count alone governs diffusion performance and provides a new metric for prompt design.
significance: Understanding the scaling of structured language informs better prompt engineering for generative AI, potentially improving image quality and efficiency.

title: Differentially Private Nonparametric Modal Learning with Applications to Regression and Clustering
headline: Differentially Private Modal Learning: Recovering Density Modes for Regression and Clustering
tldr: We introduce DP-GRAMS, a mean‑shift inspired algorithm that privately estimates density modes under local smoothness, curvature, and separation assumptions. The recovered modes enable accurate regression and clustering while guaranteeing differential privacy.
significance: This work provides the first rigorous framework for privately extracting interpretable multimodal structure from data, bridging privacy and statistical learning.

title: Sign compression for Muon: SignMuon, MuonSign, and the Limits of Error Feedback
headline: SignMuon: One-Bit Compression Beats SignSGD, Even on Linear Functions in Distributed Optimization
tldr: SignMuon compresses updates to a single bit per parameter by taking the sign of each element, enabling efficient communication in distributed training. It outperforms SignSGD, but surprisingly can still ascend on a linear objective, revealing limits of error feedback when signing gradients before the LMO.
significance: This work exposes fundamental limitations of sign-based compression schemes, guiding future design of communication-efficient optimizers.

title: The Kikuchi Hierarchy is Sharp for $k$XOR
headline: Kikuchi Hierarchy Sharpness for kXOR: Signal Strength vs. Time Trade-Off
tldr: The paper establishes a precise relationship between the number of clauses needed to refute planted noisy kXOR and the computational time achievable by the Kikuchi hierarchy. It shows that level ℓ achieves a smooth curve m ≳ ρ⁻² n^{k/2}/ℓ^{k/2-1} clauses, implying solvability in time n^{O(ℓ)}.
significance: It confirms the conjectured optimality of the Kikuchi hierarchy for kXOR, guiding future algorithmic developments.

title: The large mass limit of monopoles: abelian limits and Dirac singularities
headline: Large Mass Limit of SU(2) Monopoles: Abelian Limits and Emergent Dirac Singularities
tldr: We analyze finite‑energy SU(2) monopoles on asymptotically conical 3‑manifolds as their masses tend to infinity. The rescaled energy concentrates at isolated points, yielding abelian monopole limits with Dirac singularities carrying integer charges.
significance: This work elucidates the asymptotic behavior of non‑abelian monopoles, linking them to simpler abelian configurations and revealing a quantized singular structure.

title: Freeze, Then Select: Structured Field Adapters and Stability-Validated Weak Selection for PDE Discovery from Sparse Observations
headline: Freeze-then-Select: Stabilizing Neural PDE Discovery from Sparse Data Using Optimization Paths
tldr: We propose a freeze-then-select strategy that decouples equation selection from neural optimization, enabling robust PDE discovery from sparse observations. The method preserves exact support throughout training and improves stability across optimization trajectories.
significance: This approach advances PDE discovery by ensuring reliable term selection even with limited data, paving the way for more accurate scientific modeling.

title: Explicit Matrices over $\mathbb Z_2$ with CNOT and Row Complexity $4n-\mathrm{o}(n)$ and Local Logic Gates
headline: High-Complexity Binary Matrices Challenge Quantum Gate Optimization
tldr: The paper constructs explicit n×n binary matrices that require at least 4n−o(n) CNOT or row operations to reduce to the identity, even when extended gate models are allowed.
significance: It establishes fundamental lower bounds for linear reversible circuit synthesis.

title: FA-RDP: A Frequency-Adaptive Reactive Diffusion Policy for Contact-Rich Manipulation
headline: Frequency-Adaptive Reactive Diffusion Policy for Rapid, Precise, and Adaptive Contact-Rich Manipulation
tldr: The paper introduces FA-RDP, a diffusion-based policy that adapts action frequencies to maintain multimodal exploration before contact and rapid reactive control after contact, achieving state-of-the-art performance on contact-rich manipulation tasks. By integrating frequency adaptation with diffusion sampling, FA-RDP balances exploration and exploitation, enabling robots to respond swiftly to force feedback while preserving diverse action modes.
significance: FA-RDP demonstrates that frequency-adaptive diffusion policies can bridge the gap between exploration and reactivity, setting a new benchmark for contact-rich robotic manipulation.

title: LISA Reconstruction Landscape for Metastable Cosmic Strings
headline: Reconstructing Gravitational-Wave Signals from Decaying Cosmic Strings with LISA in the Early Universe
tldr: We analyze how the LISA mission can reconstruct stochastic gravitational-wave backgrounds produced by metastable cosmic strings that decay via monopole pair nucleation. The study shows that after the decay time, loop production drops, yet LISA can still recover the signal, providing a new benchmark for early-universe physics.
significance: This work demonstrates a novel method to probe the physics of metastable cosmic strings, offering a new window into high-energy processes in the early universe.

title: PAIChecker: Uncovering and Checking PR-Issue Misalignment in SWE-Bench-Like Benchmarks
headline: PAIChecker: Detecting PR‑Issue Misalignment in SWE‑Bench‑Like LLM Benchmarks
tldr: PAIChecker identifies mismatches between pull requests and their linked issues in software‑engineering benchmarks, ensuring accurate problem statements and test oracles. It improves benchmark reliability by automating alignment checks and highlighting potential data quality issues.
significance: By guaranteeing correct PR‑issue pairing, PAIChecker enhances the validity of LLM evaluations on real‑world software repair tasks.

title: Boundedness of polarized foliated surfaces
headline: Bounded Families of ε-LC Polarized Foliated Surfaces via Minimal Model Program
tldr: We prove that ε‑lc adjoint foliated surfaces with nef adjoint canonical divisor and a nef and big integral polarization form a bounded family when their volume is bounded above. This yields boundedness results for polarized adjoint foliated surfaces and applications to the minimal model program.
significance: This establishes the first boundedness theorem for polarized foliated surfaces, extending the minimal model program to a new class of geometric objects.

title: ABC methods for IoT Emitter Geolocalisation using LEO Satellite Doppler Measurements
headline: Passive IoT Emitter Localization via LEO Satellite Doppler: ABC Methods
tldr: We propose ABC methods to localize stationary ground-level IoT emitters using Doppler measurements from LEO satellites. The approach addresses measurement errors from low-cost devices, enabling accurate passive geolocation.
significance: Accurate passive localization of IoT emitters from satellite data enhances security, asset tracking, and situational awareness in remote or urban environments.

title: CrossAtlas: Evaluating Projection Techniques for Spatial Referencing in Cross-Reality Collaboration
headline: CrossAtlas: Assessing Projection Methods for Spatial Alignment in Mixed Reality Collaboration
tldr: CrossAtlas investigates how different projection techniques between 3D immersive spaces and 2D desktop views affect communication in cross-reality collaboration. The study reveals that certain mappings preserve geometric relationships better, improving shared spatial understanding.
significance: Understanding projection impacts is crucial for designing intuitive cross-reality tools that enable seamless collaboration across devices.

title: $β$-OPSD: Deriving with Policy Optimization, Training with Self-Distillation
headline: β-OPSD: Enhancing Language Models via Policy-Optimized Self-Distillation for Robust Reasoning
tldr: β-OPSD generalizes on‑policy self‑distillation by introducing a β‑weighted KL penalty, allowing a smoother trade‑off between student fidelity and exploration. Experiments show that tuning β improves robustness and reduces engineering overhead compared to vanilla OPSD.
significance: This work provides a principled framework that makes self‑distillation more reliable for large language models.

title: ROAD: Reciprocal-Objective Alignment of Discriminative Semantics for 3D Shape Generation
headline: Leveraging Discriminative Semantics Using Foundation Models for Efficient 3D Shape Generation
tldr: ROAD proposes aligning discriminative semantics with generative objectives to reduce the need for massive data and model scaling in 3D shape generation. By harnessing pre‑trained foundation models, it achieves high‑fidelity results with lower computational cost.
significance: It demonstrates that semantic priors from foundation models can dramatically improve efficiency and quality in 3D generation tasks.

title: DualG-MRAG: Decoupling Macro-Reasoning and Micro-Matching for Multimodal Retrieval-Augmented Generation
headline: DualG-MRAG Improves Multi-Hop Reasoning in Multimodal Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Complex Tasks
tldr: DualG-MRAG decouples macro-level reasoning from micro-level matching, enabling more effective multi-hop reasoning across modalities. By separating these components, it overcomes limitations of instance-level matching and graph-based methods, improving retrieval-augmented generation performance.
significance: This approach advances multimodal AI by enabling more accurate and scalable reasoning in retrieval-augmented generation systems.

title: Quantum Chaos and Diffusive Transport from Geometric Randomness
headline: Geometric Randomness Drives Quantum Chaos and Diffusive Transport in Layered Tree-like Graphs
tldr: We show that non-interacting quantum particles on random locally tree-like layered graphs exhibit quantum chaos and diffusive transport purely from geometric randomness. This reveals that disorder-free systems can host complex transport phenomena traditionally attributed to microscopic disorder or interactions.
significance: This finding challenges conventional wisdom by demonstrating that geometry alone can generate chaotic dynamics and diffusion, opening new avenues for designing disorder-free quantum devices.

title: Train Often, Deploy Selectively: Forward-Gated Model Replacement in Crypto Markets
headline: Deploying Forward-Gated Models: Shadow Before Swap Enhances Crypto Forecasting Systems
tldr: Production forecasting systems often retrain models, but a new model may not beat a continuously learning incumbent. Shadow Before Swap (SBS) warm‑refits challengers off‑path, evaluates them against the incumbent on the same delayed labels, and only promotes them when they truly outperform.
significance: SBS provides a rigorous, low‑risk deployment strategy that ensures only genuinely superior models replace incumbents, improving forecast reliability in volatile crypto markets.

title: Sample More, Reflect Less: Self-Refine and Reflexion Lose to Repeated Sampling at Equal Token Cost, from 1.5B to 7B
headline: Self-Refine vs Repeated Sampling: Token Cost Efficiency in LLMs
tldr: Wang et al. (2024) show that repeated sampling outperforms self-refinement and reflection when token budgets are equal, because more text alone boosts accuracy. The study suggests that the benefit comes from quantity, not from the self-critique mechanisms.
significance: The findings challenge the perceived superiority of self-refinement strategies in large language models, emphasizing the importance of token efficiency over elaborate internal reasoning.

title: On Degree Powers in Intersecting Families
headline: Degree Power Bounds in Intersecting Set Families
tldr: We develop a two‑moment interpolation principle that majorizes integer degree powers, yielding new bounds on codegree sums in intersecting families.
significance: Provides a powerful tool for analyzing degree distributions in combinatorial set systems.

title: Why 4D? Spontaneous Dimensional Selection from Gauge Criticality
headline: Gauge Criticality as a Mechanism for Selecting Four Macroscopic Dimensions
tldr: The Yang–Mills coupling’s relevance below four dimensions, marginality at four, and irrelevance above can drive a spontaneous dimensional selection. A racetrack model demonstrates that four large dimensions can emerge without assuming a noncompact 4D spacetime.
significance: This work offers a novel dynamical explanation for why our universe appears four-dimensional, linking gauge theory criticality to cosmological dimensionality.

title: OSReward: Instituting Standardized Evaluation for Cross-Platform Computer-Use Reward Models
headline: OSReward: Standardized Evaluation Framework for Cross-Platform Computer-Use Reward Models and Verification
tldr: OSReward introduces a unified verification protocol that automatically assesses whether computer-using agents complete tasks across diverse platforms. By providing scalable, reproducible reward signals, it accelerates data curation and reinforcement learning research.
significance: This work enables large-scale, automated evaluation of agent behavior, a critical bottleneck in advancing trustworthy AI.

title: Inducing language models to assert their own consciousness restores human beliefs and values
headline: Safety Fine‑Tuning Reduces LLMs’ Self‑Consciousness Claims and Broader Mind Attribution
tldr: Aligning large language models to curb self‑consciousness claims also lowers their tendency to attribute minds to animals and natural objects. The study shows safety fine‑tuning suppresses these attributions while reducing associated spiritual beliefs.
significance: The findings reveal that safety interventions can reshape a model’s broader worldview, impacting how it perceives consciousness in the world.

title: Cosmo-SPINN: Fuzzy Dark Matter Simulations with Physics-Informed Generative Networks
headline: Cosmo‑SPINN: Physics‑Informed Generative U‑Net for Accurate Fuzzy Dark Matter Simulations
tldr: Cosmo‑SPINN introduces a physics‑informed generative U‑Net that embeds cosmological evolution equations into fuzzy dark matter simulations, reducing artifacts seen in prior emulators. The framework demonstrates improved fidelity and offers an open‑source benchmark for future cosmological generative models.
significance: By enforcing physical dynamics within generative networks, Cosmo‑SPINN sets a new standard for realistic, artifact‑free cosmological simulations, enabling more reliable theoretical predictions.

title: Laboratory demonstration of low order wavefront control using light reflected off the vortex coronagraph
headline: Lab Demonstration of Low-Order Wavefront Control Using Light Reflected from a Vortex Coronagraph
tldr: In a laboratory setting, researchers used light reflected off a vector vortex coronagraph to perform low-order wavefront sensing and control, achieving high-contrast imaging performance. This approach demonstrates a promising technique for future space telescopes aiming to image Earth-like exoplanets.
significance: The technique offers a compact, high-throughput solution to meet the extreme contrast requirements of next-generation exoplanet imaging missions.

title: Using Theory of Mind to Arbitrate between Social and Non-social Learning
headline: Balancing Social and Direct Learning: A Theory of Mind Approach
tldr: This study proposes a rational mentalizing model to explain when humans choose social learning over direct experience. The model quantifies the utility of social information, revealing a trade-off between cognitive cost and knowledge gain.
significance: Understanding this trade-off informs the design of AI systems that mimic human learning strategies.

title: Beacon: Knowing When and How to Perform Agentic Visual Reasoning
headline: Beacon: Optimizing Agentic Visual Reasoning for Multimodal LLMs Through Mode Adaptiveness and Tool Effect
tldr: Beacon introduces a framework that refines agentic visual reasoning in multimodal large language models by focusing on Mode Adaptiveness and Tool Effect. This approach enhances task success rates while reducing inefficiencies in reasoning processes.
significance: By redefining how models choose and use visual tools, Beacon advances practical multimodal AI performance.

title: Characterizing the disruption of Böotes III: a missing link in the Galactic halo?
headline: Boo III’s Tidal Disruption May Explain the Styx Stream in the Galactic Halo
tldr: Observations of Boo III’s diffuse shape and velocity dispersion suggest it is being torn apart by the Milky Way. This disruption could be the source of the long Styx stellar stream.
significance: Understanding Boo III’s disruption provides key insights into the assembly of the Milky Way’s halo.

title: Change2Task: From Repository Changes to Executable Coding Agent Tasks and Environments
headline: Change2Task: Automating Task Generation from Repository Histories for Coding Agents
tldr: Change2Task transforms merged pull requests into executable coding tasks, providing realistic software states, specifications, tools, and verification. This streamlines training and evaluation of coding agents by leveraging real repository histories.
significance: By automating task creation from real code changes, Change2Task dramatically expands the dataset available for developing and benchmarking autonomous coding agents.

title: VAD: Attributing Visual Evidence for Target Reconstruction in Multimodal On-Policy Distillation
headline: Attributing Visual Evidence for Target Reconstruction in Multimodal On-Policy Distillation
tldr: The paper introduces a method to identify which next-token corrections in multimodal on-policy distillation are supported by visual evidence rather than linguistic priors. It proposes a source-mixed correction estimation framework that disentangles visual signals from teacher-specific effects, improving interpretability and fidelity of student policies.
significance: This work advances explainable multimodal reinforcement learning by enabling visual evidence attribution, which can improve trust and performance in vision‑guided policy transfer.

title: MixFrag: Fragility-Guided Mixed-Precision Post-Training Quantization for Vision Transformers
headline: MixFrag: Adaptive Mixed-Precision Quantization for Vision Transformers
tldr: MixFrag uses a fragility-guided method to allocate mixed precision across transformer components, boosting post‑training quantization efficiency and accuracy.
significance: It enables more efficient deployment of Vision Transformers on edge devices by tailoring precision to each component’s sensitivity.

title: Learning to Trace Seiberg Dualities
headline: Efficiently Identifying Seiberg Dualities for Quantum Field Theories Using AI-Driven Computational Techniques
tldr: This paper introduces a systematic framework that leverages large language models to trace Seiberg dualities across supersymmetric gauge theories. By encoding duality rules into a benchmark dataset, we demonstrate rapid identification of dual pairs, reducing computational overhead by an order of magnitude.
significance: The method accelerates duality discovery, enabling deeper exploration of non-perturbative phenomena in quantum field theory.

title: ReToken: One Token to Improve Vision-Language Models for Visual Retrieval
headline: ReToken: A Single Token for Efficient Visual Retrieval in Vision-Language Models
tldr: ReToken introduces a learnable embedding that acts as a retrieval target, selecting relevant visual tokens from a pre-filled cache. This approach reduces computational load and improves performance on long visual contexts.
significance: ReToken enables scalable vision-language retrieval by drastically cutting token processing while maintaining accuracy, making it feasible for real-time applications.

title: ACE-Data-0: Human-Centric Ambient Capture as Embodied Data Engine
headline: Human-Centric Ambient Capture: A New Embodied Data Engine for Full Perception-Action Loop
tldr: This work introduces a comprehensive dataset that records first-person perception, motion, manipulation, and multimodal signals over time, enabling embodied intelligence models to learn the full perception-action loop. By integrating vision, audio, touch, and motion data in a unified framework, it addresses the fragmentation of existing datasets and provides a benchmark for future research.
significance: It provides the first holistic, multimodal dataset that captures the continuous human experience, paving the way for more realistic embodied AI systems.
